title: Infantino's future at FIFA should be decided by election, African football chief says
facts: Confederation of African Football chief Patrice Motsepe stated that Gianni Infantino's future at FIFA should be decided by elections.
The Football Association of Ireland withdrew its support for FIFA President Gianni Infantino.
Gianni Infantino faced criticism after proposing a plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
UEFA, CONCACAF, and AFC issued a joint letter criticizing Gianni Infantino's leadership at FIFA.
Multiple continental governing bodies reportedly want Gianni Infantino to resign ahead of the March 2027 election.
Patrice Motsepe serves concurrently as a FIFA vice-president and the president of the Confederation of African Football.
Patrice Motsepe met with UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin in Salzburg during the UEFA Super Cup.
UEFA threatened to boycott the World Cup and Club World Cup in protest against Gianni Infantino's investment plan.
Patrice Motsepe maintained that Gianni Infantino did not breach rules because the investment proposals required member approval.
Gianni Infantino apologized for the manner in which the World Cup investment proposals were handled.
The English Football Association had previously withdrawn its backing for Gianni Infantino.
The Welsh Football Association had previously withdrawn its backing for Gianni Infantino.
FIFA consists of 211 national member associations that hold voting power in presidential elections.
The Football Association of Ireland rescinded its earlier letter of support following a formal board meeting.
The Football Association of Ireland cited concerns regarding governance, transparency, and consultation at FIFA.
